qualification.status: Light qualification. Built from this clean Cubature commit as Java 25 bytecode with CleanroomGradle against Cleanroom 0.7.14-alpha. The seven commits since b1140175 change only the client and the lab: the build pool takes snapshots ahead of its threads for as many jobs as they finish between two frames (measured, at most 16 a thread), its submit and poll admit without checking every held task for staleness, the client cube source counts its snapshots and cube copies with their time, and it lets go of a cube's copy no snapshot has asked for in 200 ticks (clientKeptCopyTicks), about 650 MiB less live heap at radius 20; and the lab prepares instances on ZGC with a fixed 8 GiB heap (zgc-fixed) in place of g1-ship8. The jar differs from 45e636a6's only in MODIFICATIONS.md. All 368 Java sources in the sources artifact match the commit, and core (589) tests pass. Under Quadrature's near terrain on a radius-20 tour a new place meshes in 24 to 26 s against 37 to 44 s, with the picture unchanged against the game (17 of 17 views). Generation, delivery and server code are unchanged.
qualification.contents: Bounded native generation, regional preparation, previews, storage and DH delivery; host-owned build pools available before biome-provider construction and preserved after adoption; save-level derived-data directory requests; cached cube classification and surface bands, used to install EMPTY cubes without generation and to order delivery visible-first; early initial light and surface tracking for empty sky cubes; retained-column preparation and urgent held teleports; exclusive server-thread phase accounting, with block ticks and player-map bookkeeping separated (the lab alone wraps vanilla call sites for network and tick-event phases), and client native-capture counters; regional preparation around spawn while no player is present; flushes that write each region's backlog in one batch, storage compression on reused deflaters and bounded workers, and regenerable empty cubes left unsaved; chunk-mesh builders that start with small layer buffers; a public random-tick listener API on the cubic pass; entity chunk-loading tickets that keep their entity's cube; a client cube source API (versioned snapshots, a held box, a settled signal) with a client build pool that keeps its threads busy between frames and a client terrain-preview pool that share one governor of work permits, cut on frame and server-tick p95 and raised on queued work, each logging why; a terrain preview's own small build pool, stopped with it; every client pool logging a stop line as its world goes, and counting its threads still alive 1, 2, 5 and 10 seconds after while any is; a client governor that rests while no world is attached; an optional delivery of only the light that changed (off by default); the lab's named reduced view profiles below its baseline, fixed when an instance is prepared; Mixin configurations registered through a CleanMix connector, with MixinExtras wraps and Expressions in place of redirects and constant modifiers; no compatibility code for mods or platforms outside the runtime (Demonica and its Celeritas kept), no support for clients without Cubature, no upstream code that nothing calls, of the vanilla generator fixes only those a player can still reach (sapling trees and the huge mushroom), and one build (cleanroom/). Compatibility IDs, packets, save formats and the upstream DH binary are preserved.
limits: Respawn, portal and join arrivals still load their column synchronously
